items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: And Irma went in and I remember making $1,500 a week. And we stayed in there three months, 12 weeks. We broke all records.

ctx.x: I play cards. On a regular basis? Yeah, I play every time I knock off some.

See, like I play at LSU, Baton Rouge. When I soon I get in town, I stop at the coach table. See, they had the gambling. It was wide open on the cards. They talking about gambling casinos? Gambling casinos. Gambling all night, all day. All day and all night. But anyway, that's how. That's how I would still have my faculty enough. I had a family that I had to take care of. But really what helped me is when, what we didn't get to with Irma. When Irma and I went in the Marriott.
Okay, that was, you know, 73? Yeah, 73.
Getting back to Rick, did you end your relationship with Rick because Mr. Ruffino died? No.

Okay. Here's how I ended my relationship with Rick. You see, Joe and I were pretty good buddies. We were friends. I was one of the artists who would go up there and meet him and talk all day about the business, even though he wasn't fair with the money. But I still liked him and I guess he liked me because I go there and sit down and talk with him. But anyway, things had got a little bad and we wasn't doing nothing. So I asked him, I said, well, man, look, why don't you give me a release and let me go somewhere…

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: I'm going to tell you the exact words that Irma said, she said, I wish some blacks would hire me.

ctx.x: Because you don't work, you know, to black audiences, I'm saying, you were working to whites, did blacks ever tell you, you know, why don't you play for your own kind?

No. No, no, never, no. You never get that. The only thing, and I'm going to tell you the exact words that Irma said, she said, I wish some blacks would hire me. But they don't even call Irma. Now, she played for the Zulus. And they were highly dissatisfied with her.
